summary: Repair 94/-497-498 and store it as a reference
rationale: The stray hyphen after the slash makes the locator malformed and leaves it in note instead of refs. The first sentence is verified at 94/497 and the conditional continuation at 94/498. Store 94/497-498 as the text reference alongside grammar page 570 and clear this note.

summary: Restore first-person ebi in the misfortune example
rationale: 44/108 has “maqəṯleli ebi”, referring to the speaker. The entry has third-person ebe instead; this is a person-ending difference, not orthographic normalization.

summary: Remove the unsupported third-person agent from the translation
rationale: The supplied text reads “maqəṯleli ebi” and the edition translates “die Gott mir zustoßen läßt”. The misfortune befalls the speaker; there is no additional “by him” participant.

summary: Restore the masculine actor ending in maqiṯole
rationale: 94/498 reads “Haka maqiṯole eba”. The called player throws his stick in 94/497 and is freed if he hits the horn in 94/498. The entry changes the final actor ending from -le to -la.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 3 in Imperativ (JTM 1.5/13)

data.turoyo: <...> u stad gdumarwo lu šagərti ḥreno, gdumarwo: "Hat nfaḥ maqəṯ i nuro."
data.translation: <...> sagte der Meister zu dem anderen Gesellen: Du, fach an, schüre das Feuer an.

rationale: First III Imperativ box, concrete ignition instruction.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 1.5/23)

data.turoyo: <...> w gšuqliwo qayse, aṣ ṣopatani, lašan aq qayse d mitaqəṯwo, mitaḥətwo b gawayye <...>
data.translation: <...> man kaufte Brennholz und legte es hinein, um es in diesen Öfen anzuzünden. <...>

rationale: First III Detransitive Infectum-wa, affected wood rather than ignition causer.

summary: New sense 2b: an etwas befestigen, anheften (mit b-)
rationale: Ornaments are hung on and then sewn to a tail; sustained attachment is more specific than the brief striking/contact in III.2. One attestation; exact contribution of sewing remains a question.

evidence.cite: MAC NE Old woman and a fox/29

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) angezündet werden
rationale: Wood is the affected participant of mitaqəṯwo, not an agent causing ignition. First supplied III Detransitive attestation.

summary: New sense 9: (mit l- und d-Satz) dazu kommen, Gelegenheit haben, etwas zu tun

data.gloss: (mit l- und d-Satz) dazu kommen, Gelegenheit haben, etwas zu tun

rationale: Four clauses place an action expressed by d- after a recipient-coded qyṯ. Unlike the nominal allotted share in 7, this construction expresses access to an action. Necessity in the machine rendering of 792 is not established by the Turoyo alone.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/43)

data.turoyo: L Aloho mfarfsole yaʕni b iḏayye. Gdəwewo i naqlayo, gqayṯiwo b ḥḏoḏe, gməqṭalwo alfo zlamat.
data.translation: Gott hat sie auseinander gehalten (ließ es nicht zu einem Kampf kommen). Wäre es dazu kommen, hätten sie gekämpft, 1000 Menschen wären gestorben.
data.ref: Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/43

rationale: Fills I.1 Infectum-wa with reciprocal clash in a counterfactual condition.

evidence.cite: Bilgic Die Rolle Məḏyaḏs im Tur Abdin/43

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit Intransitive (JL 14.8/4)

data.turoyo: <...> Bi=nfalto d nafilo, riša qayəṯ bi=čmənto du=darbo. Tamo riša twir. <...>

rationale: Fills I.3 Preterit Intransitive with body-part subject and concrete impact.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/61)

data.turoyo: U ḥa, d koḏəʕ, kmanṭele stimbar, gdoyəq buwe basmore bi xaṣrayo w bayo, kəmʕaləq aʕ ʕaqudani, d lo d qayṯi b ḥḏoḏe w lo məqṭəʕ u šəriṭo d taḥtayye. <...>
data.translation: Wer sich auskennt, holt sich ein Brett aus Pappelholz, schlägt auf beiden Seiten Nägel ein und hängt dann die Süßwürste so auf, dass sie sich nicht berühren und dass die Schnur, an der sie hängen nicht reißt. <...>

summary: example for sense 6 in Infectum-wa (JTM 2.3/6)

data.turoyo: W sayminawo hanək ste ḥašwo w maye d baḏənǧan, liʔannu lo qaṯwo, yaʕni latwo tamo bu saṯwo baḏənǧan ʕadi d maḥtina, taza <...>
data.translation: Wir bereiteten für sie eine Füllung zu, und fügten Tomatenmark hinzu, denn man konnte dort im Winter keine normalen frischen Tomaten finden, die man hätte nehmen können. <...>

rationale: First I.6 Infectum-wa cell: seasonal availability, with explanatory absence clause.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 2.8/2)

data.translation: <...> Wir pflegten den Reis sorgfältig zu waschen, den wir zuvor ins heiße Wasser gelegt hatten. Dann ließen wir ihn abtropfen, gaben ihn in den Kochtopf auf das Butterschmalz und rührten ihn vorsichtig um, bis er nicht aneinander klebte.

rationale: Fills I.1 Infectum with rice adhesion; participant extension of sticking.

summary: example for sense 7 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 3.2/6)

data.translation: <...> Sie fanden eine Gelegenheit, jeder der diese Gelegenheit hatte, floh nach ʿIwardo.

rationale: Fills I.7 Preterit Intransitive with an opportunity allotted to a recipient.

summary: example for sense 8 in Infectum (JTM 5.3/45)

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/45)

data.translation: »O Gott!« sagte Dschauhar, »könnte ich doch eine Cigarette haben«. Da holte einer vom Gefolge drei Cigaretten aus seiner Tasche und gab sie dem Dschauhar.

rationale: Fills I.6 Preterit Intransitive with paired negative and positive availability; decision for the second token shares this quotation.

data.translation: "Aber wenn mir der Kater zufällt, so mag ich ihn nicht." "Wer weiss", sagte der Marder, "wem der Kater zu Teil werden wird."

rationale: Fills I.7 Infectum with prospective allotment and l-recipient.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (PrS 87/6)

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum (30/161)

rationale: Fills I.3 Infectum with overt indicative prefix and feminine hand subject.

data.translation: Am Abend sprach er zu seinen, Brüdern: "Ich kann einen so weiten Weg nicht allein gehen. Vielleicht stoße ich nicht so schnell auf das Heilmittel; kommt mit mir, wir wollen alle dreigehen!"

rationale: Fills I.6 Infectum with implicit remedy theme and l-finder.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum (75/256)

data.translation: Es vergingen ein Paar weitere Monate, da sprach er: "Ich bitte Gott, daß deinen Vater eine Krankheit befallen möge, für die es kein Heilmittel gibt außer Löwenmilch in Löwenhaut, von einem Löwengeschleppt.»

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (94/506)

data.turoyo: Faqat, i naqqa d ḥa m an naʕime d moḥela, d əzzá i qarno, d qayṯo b qatoro, b nošo, b šuro aw b mən, d qayṯo, aḥ ḥawrone ḥrene kəmmi: “Sar!”
data.translation: Wenn aber einer der Jungen das Horn schlägt, und es an einem großen Stein, einem Menschen, an einer Mauer oder sonst etwas anschlägt, so rufen die anderen Spielkameraden kurdisch. Kalt!

rationale: Fills I.3 Infectum with one full clause covering both repeated contact tokens.

data.translation: Dann eilte er in die Stadt, holte so viele schöne Dinge zum essen, als es nur gab, und machte ein essen, wie es nicht einmal in den Gasthäusern und selbst nicht bei den Paschas zu finden ist.

summary: I contact is nonagentive with a b-/l-/ʕal-target; III contact adds a causer and affected item. Reciprocal b-ḥḏoḏe covers literal touching, sticking and conflict, with the head variant recorded separately as an idiom.

I finding and allotment place the acquired theme/event as subject and recipient in l-. Opportunities, food and adverse events show the boundary; no transitive finder is inferred from the German translation.
Ignition contrasts I burning/catching fire, III causing it, and III Detransitive affected wood. Part act. burning under pāš/fayišo is a continuing state, not another ignition event.

Contracted qaṯ, qōṯ and qaṯwo are preserved. Context may distinguish Preterit Intransitive from Infectum, but the spelling alone is not conclusive. The two qāṯ in the same allocation verse remain separate occurrence decisions.
MM 95, prs 141/11, the shark at prs 115/13, 69/393, 69/501 and the MAC lamp recording already have examples; they are not re-added merely to fill a thin cell.
Jan passages here are predominantly interviews and dialogue. Reduced qaṯ-/qoṯ-/quyaṯ- coexist with full qayəṯ-/qoyəṯ-, so register should not be called uniformly learned written prose.

Recipient l- occurs with finding, allocation, affliction and the access-to-action construction. It is not automatically an agent or a direct object: numeral coin themes and postposed feminine nouns particularly need checking.

maqəṯiwola with a candle theme and a shrine beneficiary separates theme from beneficiary. I.5 contrasts b-targets and l-affected people; I.3 includes the stones striking speakers rather than merely touching them.

qayəṯwo, qayṯiwo and contracted qaṯwo do not by themselves prove a habitual/anterior distinction. The reader's full-form Preterit-wa labels are retained where supported by spelling; contracted cases remain explicitly provisional.
No existing glossary example is corrected on the authority of Jan machine English. A possible proverb in Jan 4.I/199 is held pending interpretation; scoped safruno search found no matching idiom.

Does III maqəṯla in the tail-ornament context itself imply fastening, or does the following sewing predicate add fixation? Subsense 2b is based on one occurrence.
Confirm contracted qaṯwo as Infectum-wa in JTM 2.3/6 and plural agreement of III Detransitive mitaqəṯwo in JTM 1.5/23.

Check bare qayṯi (PrS 87/6), plural-looking qaṯṯe with blows, masculine qayəṯle with feminine fərṣa, and the negation in 94/499.
Verify whether Qəṯla (Jan 2.4/1088) belongs to qyṯ at all; no new I Preterit box is proposed from this opaque form.
In Jan 4.I/525, are the coins the subject of 'accrue to', or objects of 'touch/spend'? Confirm the segmentation of koqoyaṯṯe before adding a spending sense.
Clarify the defective clause qayəṯ harke (Jan 4.I/560) and the unspecified subject of kqoyaṯla (Jan 4.II/889). Both analyses remain unresolved.

Does access construction 9 also express obligation in Jan 4.II/792? The repeated positive/negative opportunity clauses support access but not a general necessity gloss.

rationale: Sense 1 describes something befalling someone: the verb is widerfahren. Wiederfahren is a spelling error in this meaning.

summary: Mutual contact includes rice grains sticking and horses clashing, without new senses for the participant type.
Availability can be predicated of tomatoes or food with no expressed recipient.
Unheil bala is the adverse subject in the same l-affected construction as disease; this extends the event noun, not a new form.
Electrical activation already occurs in the inherited gloss examples; qalorifer extends the appliance object beyond lighting.
Miraculous fingers appear as burning/luminous subjects in a candle comparison.

Kin branches and individual captives occur as allocated subjects after explicit pəšk. First-person qayəṯno and feminine qayiṯo preserve personal agreement; the baseline plus round 1 already has five Preterit Intransitive examples.
Companions, food and employment extend availability rather than distribution by lot; Jan corroborates round-1 availability without an overt recipient.
Reciprocal conflict with collective human subjects confirms the round-1 b-qarʕe d-ḥḏoḏe idiom; no duplicate idiom or separate village sense.
miqrob is the infective subject, extending the disease participant rather than creating a distinct spreading sense.
Incense occurs as ignited material beside candles; the change of substance does not establish a new sense.
Psychological impact is a possible figurative participant extension, provisionally retained without a new numbered sense.
